headline: This morning's showers have passed without trouble and no model shows a flooding burst before Monday: the channel crested at 0.53 ft at Caltrain and is falling, and only light rain is expected Saturday night.

summary.text: The morning burst is over: HRRR's wettest 3 hours ahead fell from 0.31 in this morning to 0.06 in. The channel peaked at 0.53 ft at Caltrain and is back to 0.11 ft.
Wettest 3 hours, next 72 h: NBM 0.10, ECMWF 0.09 (Sat night), HRRR 0.06, GFS 0.06, RRFS 0.02. Consensus about 0.08 in, mostly the tail of this morning's showers.
No street flooding expected through Monday morning. Yellow (garage) needs about 0.71 in in 3 hours or a 0.40 in hour; nothing comes close.
Coastal Flood Advisory for the Bay shore until 11 AM Saturday; tides running about 1.5 ft above prediction. NWS expects a Coastal Flood Warning as king tides arrive next week.
Nothing needed today. Use the weekend or Monday's dry day to clear street drain grates and yard drains and check sandbags before Tuesday's storm.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: The shower bands that crossed the Peninsula this morning are pushing south, with clearing behind them this afternoon and evening (NWS San Francisco update, 7:52 AM). A weaker system brings light showers to the Bay Area late Saturday afternoon into Sunday; NWS expects only a tenth to a quarter inch from Saturday to early Monday, but notes that nearly saturated soils make nuisance flooding more likely if a stronger shower develops. Monday is the dry day. A stronger, negatively tilted trough arrives Tuesday into Wednesday with possible thunderstorms and moderate to heavy rain, during next week's king tides. That storm is still just beyond this discussion's 72-hour window, so this is a quiet note until it gets closer.

sections.title: What changed and model trends
sections.text:
Since the 7:25 AM discussion the morning burst has come and gone. The HRRR 15-minute output had about 0.26 in in an hour around 7 AM; the Caltrain rain gauge recorded 0.04 in in each of the hours ending 6 and 7 AM, nothing near the 0.40 in alarm. The hourly HRRR is back in this snapshot (8 AM run), and from 10 AM on its wettest 3 hours are 0.06 in, essentially the last showers this morning. Its 15-minute output shows only a few hundredths of an inch Saturday evening and night.

Other models for the next 72 hours (wettest 3 hours / total): NBM 0.10 / 0.13 in, ECMWF 0.09 / 0.19 in (Saturday 7 to 10 PM), GFS 0.06 / 0.12 in, RRFS 0.02 / 0.06 in (10 PM Thu run). HRRR's total is 0.10 in to the end of its run early Sunday.

Consensus (HRRR 0.06 × 1.25, RRFS 0.02, NBM 0.10): about 0.08 in, down from 0.14 in. That looks right; even a heavy shower cell on Saturday night would have to be several times stronger than any model shows to matter.

sections.title: Tide and the channel
sections.text:
NOAA's Bay model keeps running about 1.5 ft above the predicted tides. This morning's 7.9 ft high at 8:32 AM peaked near 9.6 ft on the model. Tonight's 6.4 ft high at 9:15 PM runs about 8.1 ft; Saturday's 8.4 ft high at 9:06 AM about 9.9 ft. Saturday evening's light rain falls on the low (0.3 ft at 4:05 PM, about 1.8 ft on the model) and the rising tide toward the 6.6 ft high at 10:19 PM (about 8.2 ft). The model run ends 1 AM Sunday; Sunday's 8.8 ft and Monday's 9.2 ft morning highs are not yet covered.

NWS has a Coastal Flood Advisory for Bayshore locations until 11 AM Saturday (up to 1.4 ft of inundation in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways, up to 1.8 ft of surge) and expects to upgrade the Bays to a Coastal Flood Warning as the king tides approach.

Channel: upstream of Caltrain the gauge rose with the morning showers to 0.53 ft at 8:19 AM, near the high tide, and has fallen to 0.11 ft at 9:49 AM (Flood Monitoring 2.8 ft). At Alameda de las Pulgas it touched 0.37 ft at 7:35 AM and reads 0.24 ft at 9 AM (Flood Monitoring 3.18 ft).

sections.title: Current observations
sections.text: The Caltrain rain gauge's last tip was at 7:45 AM: nothing in the last hour, 0.04 in over 3 hours, 0.12 in over 6 hours and 0.28 in over 24 hours. The channel is low and falling.

sections.title: What to do
sections.text:
• No need to move cars.
• Use the weekend or Monday's dry day to clear leaves from street drain grates and yard drains and check sandbags: Tuesday and Wednesday bring heavier rain on top of the king tides.
• Cold mornings Saturday. Don't drive or walk through moving water.
